title: Partition Labels
keyIdea: A part must contain every copy of each letter in it. Record each letter's last index; scan with end = max(end, last[s[i]]). When i == end, nothing in the current part appears later, so cut there. Cutting as early as possible gives the most parts.

approaches.name: Greedy with last occurrence
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). last[c] = last index of c; scan, extend end, cut when i == end and push end − start + 1.
approaches.why: Two passes; the last array has 26 entries.

quiz.q: When is it safe to cut after index i?
options: When i is the last occurrence of every letter seen in the current part (i == end)

quiz.q: Why does cutting as early as possible give the most parts?
options: Each cut is at the first legal place, so later parts get as much room as possible
